children: September saw the slowest pace of rent decline in three years, Realtor.com says. Today's rental market is being shaped by the cooling of the supply wave in the Sun Belt, renters moving to more affordable alternatives, and AI-driven job growth in the Bay Area. The median asking rent for studio, one- and two-bedroom properties across the 50 largest U.S. metros fell 0.4% year over year to $1,694. This marks the 38th consecutive month of annual declines. Nearly 43.9% of rental listings across the 50 largest metros offered a concession in September, up 1.3 percentage points from a year earlier. The strongest rent growth is in the Bay Area. Median asking rent in San Jose rose 6% to a new high of $3,565, while San Francisco rent increased 4.8% to $3,057. (chris.wack@wsj.com)
